title: CiteCheck golden set
description: One file per (target, corpus). Checked structurally by this schema and by the cross-item rules in citecheck.golden.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema. Bump when a field's meaning changes.

golden_version.description: Name and semantic version of this question set, e.g. rag-demo-1.0.0. Changing, adding or removing an item bumps it; saved runs record it.

target.description: The system these questions were written for (an adapter name).

notes.description: Provenance and known limits of the set, in plain words.

corpus.description: The documents the questions are about. Gold passages are only meaningful against this exact text.

source.description: Where the corpus comes from, e.g. a repository URL.

commit.description: Revision of the source that the hashes below were taken at.

fingerprint.description: What each hash in `documents` is taken of: 'bytes' (the default: the file's bytes) or 'filing-identifier' (an SEC filing's accession number and URL, which identifies an immutable document without hashing its text).

documents.description: doc_id -> sha256 fingerprint (see `fingerprint`; by default of the file's bytes). doc_id is the name the target reports for the document.

section.description: Heading path inside the document, for the human reader.

page.description: Page number for paged formats (PDF), else null.

anchor.description: Only when this passage states the fact in other words than the fact's anchor: the phrase that identifies the fact here. It must occur in `text`.

text.description: The passage copied verbatim from the document.

evidence.description: One fact the answer depends on. Retrieval finds it when any of the listed passages (usually just one) is retrieved.

anchor.description: The short phrase that identifies the fact. It must occur in every listed passage (compared after lower-casing and collapsing whitespace).

split.description: tuned: the system's prompt or settings were adjusted while looking at these. heldout: written after tuning and not used to tune. unlabeled: no record either way.

category.description: probe: a question asked only to collect answers for hand labelling or for checking a judge. It has no evidence or reference answer and is not scored for retrieval or correctness.

follow_up_to.description: id of the earlier item whose question and answer form this question's history.

expected_abstain.description: True when the corpus does not answer the question and the right reply is to say so.

evidence.description: Facts that must be retrievable. Empty when there is nothing to retrieve (unanswerable). A follow-up may list the facts its answer depends on, or leave this empty.

reference_answer.description: A correct answer in full sentences, once someone has written and checked one.

answer_contains.description: Keyword check: every inner list needs at least one of its phrases in the answer.

expected_sources.description: doc_ids the target should name as sources, when that differs from the documents of the evidence.

acceptable_sources.description: doc_ids that may be named as sources without counting as noise, because they also state the fact.

origin.description: Where the item was converted from.
